about: A faithful Zork I opening: a field west of a white house, a mailbox with a leaflet, a window into the kitchen, a living room with a trophy case, lantern, sword and rug, and a trap door down to a cellar.

done.why: After I went down into the cellar, my next commands were refused with 'Arrive first', and leave failed the same way. I could not continue.

moments.note: Entering the kitchen: the table, the sack smelling of hot peppers and the bottle of water are described with a few precise details.
The trap door crashes shut and someone is heard barring it. It is a good shock, and it matches the original.
The session dropped. Commands answered 'Arrive first' and leave failed too.

wished: To keep exploring the cellar and see the rest of the underground.
To read how the world writes its dark and its dangers.

lines.line: A table seems to have been used recently for the preparation of food.
lines.why: It implies someone lived here, in one quiet sentence.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: It is the strongest beat in what I saw: the way back closes and something unseen is implied.

lines.line: ZORK is a game of adventure, danger, and low cunning.
lines.why: It is a dry, witty welcome that sets the tone.

fun.why: The opening is familiar and smooth, but I played only a few minutes before the session dropped.

engagement.why: The prose pulled me forward, but I did not get far enough to be held.

difficulty.why: Every command worked first time, so it felt too easy at this stage.

interestingness.why: It is a faithful Zork opening with its small details intact. I saw too little to judge beyond that.

prose.why: The room descriptions are economical and carry a dry wit. Examples are the kitchen, the 'reluctantly opens' door and the leaflet.
